q-34957.name: Question 1
q-34957.problem: Express $\sqrt{\frac{2z}{z-1}}\,$ without radicals in the denominator.
q-34957.worked_solution:
First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{2z}{z-1}} & =\frac{\sqrt{2z}}{\sqrt{z-1}}\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the radical $\sqrt{z-1}$ from the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{z-1}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{2z}}{\sqrt{z-1}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{2z}}{\sqrt{z-1}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{z-1}}{\sqrt{z-1}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{2z}\cdot \sqrt{z-1}}{\sqrt{z-1}\cdot \sqrt{z-1}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{2z(z-1)}}{{(\sqrt{z-1})}^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{2z(z-1)}}{z-1}\end{aligned}
$$

q-34957.html:
Question 1
?

Express 2zz−1 without radicals in the denominator.

a
2z(z−1)z+1
b
2z(z+1)z−1
c
−2z(z−1)z−1
d
2z(z+1)z+1
e
2z(z−1)z−1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals: 2zz−1=2zz−1

To remove the radical z−1 from the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by z−1 and simplify:

2zz−1=2zz−1⋅z−1z−1=2z⋅z−1z−1⋅z−1=2z(z−1)(z−1)2=2z(z−1)z−1

q-34960.name: Question 2
q-34960.problem: Express $\sqrt{\frac{m+10}{m-10}}\,$ without radicals in the denominator.
q-34960.worked_solution:
First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{m+10}{m-10}} & =\frac{\sqrt{m+10}}{\sqrt{m-10}}\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the radical $\sqrt{m-10}$ from the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{m-10}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{m+10}}{\sqrt{m-10}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{m+10}}{\sqrt{m-10}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{m-10}}{\sqrt{m-10}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{m+10}\cdot \sqrt{m-10}}{\sqrt{m-10}\cdot \sqrt{m-10}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{(m+10)(m-10)}}{(\sqrt{m-10})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{{m}^{2}-{10}^{2}}}{m-10} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{{m}^{2}-100}}{m-10}\end{aligned}
$$

q-34960.html:
Question 2
?

Express m+10m−10 without radicals in the denominator.

a
m2−10m+10
b
m2−100m−10
c
m2−10m−10
d
m2+100m+10
e
m−100m−10
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals: m+10m−10=m+10m−10

To remove the radical m−10 from the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by m−10 and simplify:

m+10m−10=m+10m−10⋅m−10m−10=m+10⋅m−10m−10⋅m−10=(m+10)(m−10)(m−10)2=m2−102m−10=m2−100m−10

q-77869.name: Question 3
q-77869.worked_solution:
First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{5}{2x}} & =\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{2x}}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to remove the radical $\sqrt{2x}$ from the denominator. To do this, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{2x},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{5}}{\sqrt{2x}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2x}}{\sqrt{2x}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{10x}}{(\sqrt{2x})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{10x}}{2x}\end{aligned}
$$

q-77869.html:
Question 3
?

Rationalize the denominator of 52x.

a
10x2x
b
10xx
c
10x5x
d
5xx
e
5x2x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, we apply the quotient rule and put the numerator and denominator under separate radicals: 52x=52x

Now, we need to remove the radical 2x from the denominator. To do this, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by 2x, and simplify:

52x⋅2x2x=10x(2x)2=10x2x
